transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I spend so long checking and fixing how I look before work that I’m missing shifts and still feel like my face looks completely wrong. It's just getting really hard to manage on my own.

Are your repeated checking or grooming behaviors mainly because you feel there is something wrong or ugly about your appearance, or are they more to relieve unwanted thoughts or fears that something bad will happen if you don’t do them?

It is definitely because I feel like my face looks completely wrong, crooked, and uneven. I'm not worried about some unrelated bad event happening; I just get so distressed by how messed up my nose looks and want to make it look less awful before anyone else sees me. I just can't bear the thought of people looking at me when I look like this.
Do you think your nose and face truly look deformed to other people, or is part of you able to recognize that this may be exaggerated or not noticeable to others?

It feels completely real and terrifying to me, and I truly believe my nose looks crooked and swollen and my face is totally uneven. I am convinced that everyone can see it immediately under those bright store lights, and even when I ask my sister and she tries to reassure me, I just can't shake the feeling that it looks completely wrong and messed up to others.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient is preoccupied with a perceived defect in appearance (nose/face looking crooked, swollen, uneven), engages in repetitive appearance-related checking and fixing behaviors, and has significant distress and occupational impairment (missing shifts). The behaviors are specifically driven by appearance concerns rather than nonspecific obsessions, supporting body dysmorphic disorder (ICD-10 F45.2 hypochondriacal disorder category, which includes dysmorphophobia). Insight appears poor/delusional, but the core diagnosis remains F45.2.
